newsitem.title: UK: Clarke tells Labour to own up on privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Clarke tells Labour to own up on privatisation.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer, Kenneth Clarke, on Thursday challenged the opposition Labour Party to come clean on its plans for privatisation, particularly for air traffic control.
Clarke told reporters that Labour, in what he said was a last-minute U-turn, had decided to sell off air traffic control to help balance the public finances.
"They are treating the electorate with complete contempt if they deny they have a total and utter change of mind," he said.
Labour's Treasury spokesman Alistair Darling said on Thursday morning that Labour would have to consider privatising air traffic control because of the poor state of government finances.
Clarke said that to be in favour of privatisation just to raise money was to miss the point.
"We've improved the quality of service and lowered the cost to consumers" through the privatisation programme, he said.

Clarke also attacked Labour because of comments from the opposition party's chief economic spokesman, Gordon Brown, on Wednesday's report from an independent think-tank, the Institute for Fiscal Studies.
Clarke denied the report showed the average household was seven pounds per week worse off.
"What the report said is that people are better off and when people are better off they pay more tax. These figures have been ludicrously misused by Gordon Brown," he said.
